title: Bomb Blast at Manipur BJP MLA's Residence Condemned as 'Attack on Democracy'
excerpt: An explosive device detonated at the Imphal home of BJP MLA Sapam Ranjan Singh in the early hours of Friday, with the chief minister calling it a 'senseless and barbaric' attack.
body:
• A bomb exploded at the Imphal West residence of BJP MLA and state government spokesperson Sapam Ranjan Singh around 1:30 AM Friday, causing no injuries
  • Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited the site and condemned the attack as "senseless and barbaric" and an "attack on democracy"
  • The MLA had returned from New Delhi a day earlier after meetings with central leaders on Manipur's security situation
  • Security forces separately arrested five militants from banned outfits across three districts in coordinated operations within 24 hours

A bomb blast shook the residence of BJP MLA and Manipur government spokesperson Sapam Ranjan Singh in the early hours of Friday, in an attack the state's chief minister called "senseless and barbaric" and an assault on democracy.

The explosion occurred around 1:30 AM at the rear of Singh's residence in Konthoujam Mayai Leikai, a densely populated residential area in Imphal West district, NDTV reported. The blast left a small crater on the ground and caused minor damage to the compound walls. No injuries were reported.

MLA Had Returned From Delhi Meetings

Singh, who also served as a former state minister, said the blast was powerful enough to shake his house. "There was a loud sound, and initially we thought the incident had taken place somewhere very close to my house. We later came to know that the blast had occurred behind my house, within my campus," he told reporters.

https://x.com/ndtv/status/2093399615085347204

The MLA said he had not received any prior threats. He had returned to Imphal on Thursday from New Delhi, where he held meetings with central leaders over issues concerning the security situation in Manipur, and had met local party workers that evening.

"What is Manipur gaining from such acts? What is the purpose? Without any reason, carrying out bomb attacks or any kind of secret violent activities."

— Sapam Ranjan Singh, MLA, Konthoujam

Chief Minister Visits Site

Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited the MLA's residence following the blast and took stock of the situation. He condemned the attack in the strongest terms.

"I strongly condemn such senseless and barbaric attack on the residence of a people's representative. This act of violence is an attack on our democracy and the perpetrators will be brought to justice soon," the chief minister said on social media.

Local Meira Paibis — women's civil society groups that have been at the forefront of protests in Manipur — staged a sit-in at the MLA's residence, condemning the blast and demanding immediate government action. The protesters expressed particular concern that the attack occurred in a densely populated area where an explosion could have caused serious civilian casualties.

Five Militants Arrested in Separate Operations

In a separate development, security forces arrested five militants from multiple banned outfits across three Manipur districts within 24 hours, officials said on Friday, according to IANS.

The coordinated operations by Manipur Police, Assam Rifles, and other central forces led to arrests in Imphal West, Imphal East, and Kakching districts. The detained individuals belong to four banned organizations: the People's Liberation Army and its political wing, the Revolutionary People's Front; the United People's Party of Kangleipak; and the United National Liberation Front.

According to police, the detainees were reportedly involved in attacks on civilians, kidnapping, forcible collection of so-called "subscriptions," and recruiting youths into the proscribed groups.

Renewed Security Concerns

The attack has renewed concerns over the safety of elected representatives and civilians in Manipur, which has been wracked by ethnic violence and militancy. Police have registered a case and launched an investigation into the blast. No group has claimed responsibility.

The incident is being viewed in the context of ongoing tensions in the northeastern state, which has seen periodic flare-ups of violence. Authorities are reviewing security arrangements for elected representatives in the wake of the bombing, according to local media reports.
nri_angle: The security situation in Manipur remains a concern for the Indian diaspora, particularly those from the northeast, as violence against elected representatives signals continued instability.
